cards.text: This is the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite, and it's a burden against Nineveh, the same great city Jonah once warned (Jonah 3:3-4). Nahum doesn't warm up with small talk, friend. He goes STRAIGHT to who God is.
First line out of the gate: the LORD is a jealous and avenging God, full of wrath, who takes vengeance on His foes. And this is the same God Jonah once called gracious and compassionate (Jonah 4:2).

cards.question: Nahum says this jealous and avenging God is quick to anger.
The LORD is slow to anger. But what does Nahum say He will do about the guilty?

answers.text: He will forget them over time
He will let them all go free

cards.text: Then Nahum paints a picture: His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet. Friend, I'd be standing there holding my chef's hat on with my MUSTACHE.

cards.question: When the LORD rebukes the sea, Nahum says He makes it ___.

cards.text: He makes all the rivers run dry, and Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts. I've watched dough dry out on the counter, friend, but whole RIVERS?

cards.question: When the LORD shows up, what does Nahum say the mountains do?

cards.text: Then Nahum asks, "Who can endure His burning anger?" His wrath is poured out like fire, and friend, I flinch just opening a hot oven door.

cards.question: Nahum says that before the LORD's burning anger, even rocks are shattered.

cards.text: Then, right in the middle of all that storm and fire, Nahum says the LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress. It's like a storm rattling the whole street, and you've got a solid brick house to run into.

cards.question: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress. Who does Nahum say He cares for?

cards.text: Then Nahum says that with an overwhelming flood, the LORD will make an end of Nineveh.

cards.question: Nahum says the LORD will let His enemies escape into darkness.

cards.text: Then Nahum says that whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end.

cards.question: Plots against the LORD come to an end. Then Nahum talks about affliction. What does he say about it?

answers.text: It will not rise up a second time
It will come back twice as strong
It will last for many more years

cards.text: Then Nahum stacks up pictures: they'll be entangled as with thorns and consumed like the drink of a drunkard. I got my mustache tangled in a whisk ONE time, friend, and I'm still not over it.

cards.question: Nahum adds one more picture: being consumed like stubble that is fully ___.

cards.text: Then Nahum speaks right to the city: from Nineveh comes a plotter of evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.
Now the LORD Himself speaks. And when the LORD says something, friend, you put the cookie DOWN and you listen.

cards.question: The LORD talks about those who are allied and numerous. What does He say will happen to them?

answers.text: They will be cut down and gone
They will be spared this time

cards.question: Then the LORD turns to Judah, the kingdom that stayed with David's family (1 Kings 12:20). He says He has afflicted Judah, but He will afflict them no longer.
The LORD says He will now break the ___ from Judah's neck and tear away Judah's shackles.

cards.text: Then the LORD issues a command concerning Nineveh.

cards.question: The LORD's command says Nineveh will have descendants to carry on its name.

cards.text: He will also cut off the carved image and cast idol from the house of Nineveh's gods.

cards.question: No descendants and no idols. What does the LORD say He will prepare for Nineveh?

cards.text: Then Nahum says look to the mountains: here come the feet of someone bringing good news, proclaiming peace. I know that feeling, friend: after years in the back of a junk drawer, I got called out with good news too.

cards.question: Good news and peace are on the way. What does Nahum tell Judah to do?
Nahum tells Judah the wicked will never again march through them.
